now.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
now.text: Miguel travels to Earth-6799 to explain the multiverse to its Spider-Man. Instead the two get stuck arguing and pointing at each other.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Earth-6799's Spider-Man, who ends up arguing with Miguel.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A visitor Peter ends up arguing with.

proposed.text: Miguel travels to Earth-67 to explain the multiverse to its Spider-Man. Instead the two get stuck arguing and pointing at each other.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Earth-67's Spider-Man, who ends up arguing with Miguel.

changes.evidence: In the Into the Spider-Verse post-credits scene Miguel O'Hara goes to Earth-67 (the film's own name for that universe), not Earth-6799. Earth-6799 is the Marvel Database's label for the separate 1967 TV show universe.

owner_calls.question: Stage 0 (Marvel Zombies, first episode) is built only on Kamala's nightmares of a red figure. In the next episode Blade says Wanda is deliberately sending these visions into her mind. Should a vision that Wanda sends on purpose count as an event between them, or does the rule that visions and dreams are not events mean this stage should go, so their story starts at Marvel Zombies#3?
options: Keep stage 0: Wanda sending visions on purpose is a real act
Drop stage 0 and start the connection at Marvel Zombies#3
Keep it, but move it to Marvel Zombies#2, where Blade names Wanda as the one sending the visions
owner_calls.evidence: In episode 1 Kamala dreams of a nightmarish red figure. In episode 2 Blade tells her Wanda Maximoff has her in her sights and is sending visions into her mind. They first meet in person at New Asgard in episode 3.
